title: Fox et al. 2014, ApJ — Uncovering the B-star companion of SN 1993J (states the defining IIb property and that 1993J is the prototype)
content: The Type IIb supernova (SN IIb; see Filippenko 1997 for a review) subclass exhibits spectroscopic evidence for hydrogen emission at early times (the defining property of Type II supernovae, SNe II), He I absorption at later times (as in SNe Ib), and renewed broad H-alpha emission in the nebular phase. The Type IIb supernova (SN) 1993J is one of only a few stripped-envelope supernovae with a progenitor star identified in pre-explosion images.

citations.used_for: template_match(sn1993j_iib_prototype, plus4_days): top SNID template = SN 1993J (the IIb prototype) at +4d. SN 1993J is the canonical Type IIb prototype, included as a IIb template in the SNID/CfA template library. A top template match to SN 1993J at the correct epoch is strong evidence for IIb. ROOT classification of SN1993J as IIb is grounded (Filippenko et al. 1993; reaffirmed Fox et al. 2014), and its inclusion as a SNID IIb template is grounded (Liu & Modjaz / Modjaz et al. 2014 SNID template set). However NO published numeric LR for 'top template = 1993J -> IIb' exists. Direction strongly favors IIb. Honest verdict: direction_only.->type_iib_supernova
